title: CVE-2026-102764: Critical BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Exploited by China-Linked Hackers
content_md: BeyondTrust has disclosed CVE-2026-102764, a critical vulnerability in Remote Support (RS) that was exploited as a zero-day by a suspected China-nexus cyber espionage actor. The flaw carries a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3 and can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to perform arbitrary file operations on a vulnerable appliance. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant attribute the observed exploitation to ARMORY CASTLE, formerly tracked as UNC5221 and also associated with the name WARP PANDA. The group has a history of targeting internet-facing security appliances and exploiting previously unknown vulnerabilities to gain persistent access to high-value environments. The attacks began as early as August 29, 2026, when the threat actor successfully exploited one BeyondTrust-hosted Remote Support instance and one self-hosted appliance. BeyondTrust later reproduced the vulnerability, developed a fix, and began distributing the BT26-05 patch before publicly disclosing the CVE on October 15, 2026. Successful exploitation can provide attackers with a foothold on an appliance that brokers privileged remote access and may contain or provide access to administrative credentials, API secrets, support sessions, and internal endpoints. Mandiant observed attackers escalating privileges to root, deploying custom malware, harvesting credentials, modifying access controls, and pivoting into downstream systems.
